record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Find a Hardy-field function a(t) with super-polynomial growth, meaning a(t) / t^k → ∞ for every k, such that the integer sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Find an example of a function a ∈ H that grows faster than polynomials, meaning, a(t)/t^k → ∞ for every k ∈ N, such that the sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote a Hardy field, that is, a field of germs at infinity of real-valued smooth functions defined on some half-line $[c,\infty)$ that is closed under differentiation. A function $a \in \mathcal{H}$ is said to have super-polynomial growth if
$$\lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{a(t)}{t^k} = \infty \quad \text{for every } k \in \mathbb{N}.$$
For an integer sequence $(b_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, we say that $(b_n)$ is good for multiple recurrence of powers of a single transformation if for every invertible measure-preserving system $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, every $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$, and every $A \in \mathcal{B}$ with $\mu(A) > 0$, there exists $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that
$$\mu\bigl(A \cap T^{-b_n} A \cap T^{-2 b_n} A \cap \cdots \cap T^{-\ell b_n} A\bigr) > 0,$$
and we say $(b_n)$ is good for multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation if for every such system, every $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$, and all $f_1,\dots,f_\ell \in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(T^{b_n} x)\, f_2(T^{2 b_n} x) \cdots f_\ell(T^{\ell b_n} x)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N \to \infty$.

Exhibit a function $a \in \mathcal{H}$ with super-polynomial growth such that the integer sequence $(\lfloor a(n) \rfloor)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is simultaneously good for multiple recurrence and good for multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation.
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along Hardy sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on multiple ergodic averages along Hardy field sequences (e.g., Frantzikinakis–Tsinas 2024, and Ferré Moragues–Koutsogiannis 2025 on Furstenberg systems of superpolynomial-growth sequences) addresses Hardy sequences of polynomial growth and certain superpolynomial cases, but no explicit construction has been verified that produces a Hardy-field function of super-polynomial growth whose floor sequence is simultaneously good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Multiple ergodic averages along functions from a Hardy field: convergence, recurrence and combinatorial applications
status_evidence.snippet: Confirms conjectures of Frantzikinakis on Hardy-field convergence and recurrence, with focus on polynomial-growth and mixed regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-growth Hardy sequences are addressed but super-polynomial single-transformation power case is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Furstenberg systems of certain sequences of superpolynomial growth
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Furstenberg systems for sequences of superpolynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: Treats structural properties for some superpolynomial Hardy sequences but does not exhibit a Hardy-field function of super-polynomial growth that is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers of a single transformation.
